title: Enrollment and Browser Access certificate API: wire keys, paths and client quirks

prose.text: Enrollment (signing) certificates and Browser Access certificates are separate API objects with different quirks. Browser Access certificate use is in [[zpa.browser-access.certificates]]; connector enrollment is in [[zpa.app-connectors.enrollment]].
{{ba-update-asymmetry}} Whether the Python PUT works is open {{gap:ba-certificate-put-valid}}.
The client certificate types are four in the contract and two in the Python docstring {{divergence:client-cert-type-values}}.
Whether the two values are synonyms is open {{gap:client-cert-type-synonyms}}.
The validity timestamps are integers in the contract and strings in the SDKs {{divergence:validity-epoch-types}}.
Whether the first match is the only match is open {{gap:enrollment-name-duplicates}}.

enrollment-cert-cname-wire-key.statement: The Go EnrollmentCert struct tags the canonical-name field `cName`, while the OpenAPI response schema and the Python model use `getcName`.
enrollment-cert-cname-wire-key.conditions: Whether the server also accepts `cName` is not shown by these sources; see the divergence.

enrollment-cert-lowercase-keys.statement: The private-key and session-key fields of an enrollment certificate use the all-lowercase wire keys `zrsaencryptedprivatekey` and `zrsaencryptedsessionkey`, in the Go struct, the Python model and the OpenAPI schema.

python-enrollment-model-gaps.statement: The Python EnrollmentCertificate model never reads `description` from a response and does not emit it in request_format, so a caller who serializes a model instance with request_format and sends the result loses the description; the SDK's own add and update methods send their keyword arguments as the body. Its no-config branch also names an attribute `zrsaencryptedprivate_key`, which differs from the `zrsaencryptedprivatekey` that request_format reads, so request_format on an empty instance raises AttributeError.

python-enrollment-model-gaps.conditions: Statement changed per verifier: it said any description sent through the model is dropped, but add_enrollment_cert and update_enrollment build the body from keyword arguments, and no call in enrollment_certificates.py uses request_format (read from the whole file). The absence of description from the config branch and from request_format was read from the whole model; a quote cannot prove an absence. The Go struct and the OpenAPI schema both define description.

go-no-validity-checks.statement: The Go SDK has no such validity-window or time-zone checks: its enrollment certificate writes send whatever the struct holds.
go-no-validity-checks.conditions: Rests on the three Go write functions opening with the NewRequestDo call and on a read of the whole enrollmentcert package at the pin, which converts and validates nothing; a quote cannot pin the absence.

python-validity-window-checks.statement: The Python SDK checks valid_from, valid_to and time_zone, rejecting a start more than one hour in the past, a range over 365 days, and a time zone not in the pytz list. The Go SDK's `Create`, `Update` and self-signed generate functions open by passing the certificate struct to `NewRequestDo`, with nothing before the call but allocating the response or building the path. add_enrollment_cert and generate_self_signed send the body as the keyword arguments, so the window goes out as epoch seconds in strings. update_enrollment copies the keyword arguments into a new body before converting, so it sends the raw valid_from, valid_to and time_zone and no epoch values.

quotes: raise ValueError("Start time cannot be more than 1 hour in the past.")
raise ValueError("Start time and end time range cannot exceed 1 year.")

func Create(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, cert *EnrollmentCert) (*EnrollmentCert, *http.Response, error) { v := new(EnrollmentCert) resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "POST", mgmtConfigV1+service.Client.GetCustomerID()+enrollmentCertEndpoint, nil, cert, v)

func Update(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, certID string, cert *EnrollmentCert) (*http.Response, error) { path := fmt.Sprintf("%v/%v", mgmtConfigV1+service.Client.GetCustomerID()+enrollmentCertEndpoint, certID) resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "PUT", path, nil, cert, nil)

(*GenerateSelfSignedCert, *http.Response, error) { v := new(GenerateSelfSignedCert) resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "POST", mgmtConfigV1+service.Client.GetCustomerID()+enrollmentCertEndpoint+"/selfsigned/generate", nil, cert, v)
evidence.note: the Go write functions pass the struct straight to the request with no validation

python-validity-window-checks.conditions: Statement changed per verifier: it said all Python writes send the epoch values; update_enrollment converts into kwargs after body has already copied them, and pops the raw keys from kwargs only, so its body keeps them (camel-cased by the executor, [[shared.sdk-python.request-handling:body-camel-case]]). generate_self_signed was added because it converts like add_enrollment_cert. The Go statement rests on reading the enrollmentcert package, which converts nothing and validates nothing before the request. The OpenAPI schema says validFromInEpochSec is not applicable for put and post calls because the value is extracted from the certificate.

python-delete-dry-run.statement: The Python enrollment certificate delete sends the dryRun query parameter only when dry_run is truthy, so dry_run=False is the same as omitting it.

system-provisioned-names.statement: The Go integration test asserts that GetAll returns enrollment certificates named Root, Client, Connector, Service Edge and Isolation Client.

quotes: // Check if GetAll returns specific certificate names
t.Errorf("Expected certificate with name %s not found in GetAll response", reqName)

system-provisioned-names.conditions: The test shows these names are expected in a test tenant; that they exist in every tenant or cannot be changed is not stated.

name-lookup-case-rules.statement: Enrollment certificate GetByName compares the name with strings.EqualFold, while the BaCertificate GetIssuedByName compares with ==, so a wrong-case name finds an enrollment certificate but not an issued Browser Access certificate.

enrollment-cert-microtenant-scope.statement: In the Go enrollment certificate service, Get, Delete and GetAll pass the service's microtenant ID as a filter, while Create and Update pass nil for it.

evidence.after: func Get(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, id string)

enrollment-cert-microtenant-scope.conditions: Passing nil does not mean Create and Update send no microtenantId: NewRequestDo still adds one from the body, then ZPA_MICROTENANT_ID, then the client configuration ([[zpa.terraform.data-source-selection:inject-precedence-env-over-config]]), never from the service-level microtenant that Get, Delete and GetAll use. Whether a microtenant-scoped create or update lands in the wrong scope is not shown; the struct carries a microtenantId field in the body.

enrollment-cert-allow-signing-omitempty.statement: The Go EnrollmentCert tags allowSigning with omitempty, so a false value is not sent.

ba-certificate-put-valid.title: Whether the server accepts PUT on certificate/{certificateId}
ba-certificate-put-valid.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Python update_certificate calls PUT on certificate/{certificate_id} although neither the Go SDK nor the OpenAPI document has one, so it is unverified whether the server accepts it (ledger clarifications.md#zpa-25-bacertificate-update_certificate-validity-as-an-api-operation).
ba-certificate-put-valid.blocks: telling whether Python-side Browser Access certificate updates can work

client-cert-type-synonyms.title: Whether ISOLATION_CLIENT and APP_PROTECTION are the same client certificate type
client-cert-type-synonyms.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ISOLATION_CLIENT (Python docstring) and APP_PROTECTION (recorded example) may be synonyms for the same certificate role; the contract lists both. The contract describes clientCertType as read-only and ignored on PUT and POST, so creating certificates with each value would not test it. List the existing enrollment certificates in a tenant, record the clientCertType each returns, and compare the certificates that carry each value.
client-cert-type-synonyms.blocks: choosing a client certificate type for AppProtection

enrollment-name-duplicates.title: Whether enrollment certificate names are unique and the lookup order is stable
enrollment-name-duplicates.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Go GetByName sends a search plus the active microtenant, walks the returned list and returns the first case-insensitive exact-name match without detecting a second match, so tenant-wide uniqueness of enrollment certificate names and the stability of duplicate-match order are unverified. The Python get_enrolment_by_name, added in v1.11, also takes the first case-insensitive name match from the list, so both SDKs depend on the answer. Create two enrollment certificates with the same name in a scratch tenant, if the API allows it, and call the lookup repeatedly.
enrollment-name-duplicates.blocks: trusting a name lookup of an enrollment certificate

enrollment-cname-key.summary: The enrollment certificate canonical-name key differs between the Go SDK and the OpenAPI document with the Python model.

positions.says: The Go EnrollmentCert tags the field `cName`.
The OpenAPI response schema names the property `getcName`, and the Python model reads and writes `getcName`.

enrollment-cname-key.impact: A Go caller does not read the canonical name from a response that carries `getcName`, so the value stays empty. Which key the server accepts on write is not shown. Read the raw response before relying on the Go field.

client-cert-type-values.summary: The OpenAPI enrollment certificate `clientCertType` has four values, while the Python create docstring lists two.

positions.says: The contract enum is ZAPP_CLIENT, ISOLATION_CLIENT, NONE and APP_PROTECTION, and the contract describes clientCertType as read-only: applicable only for GET calls and ignored in PUT and POST calls.

expect.description: Read only property. Applicable only for GET calls, ignored in PUT/POST calls.

positions.says: The Python create docstring lists ZAPP_CLIENT and ISOLATION_CLIENT.

client-cert-type-values.impact: The contract has both ISOLATION_CLIENT and APP_PROTECTION, so neither the Python list nor an example showing APP_PROTECTION is the full set; whether the two are synonyms is not shown. Because the contract says the server ignores clientCertType on PUT and POST, the value the Python docstring offers for create may have no effect; read the type back rather than trusting what was sent.

validity-epoch-types.summary: The OpenAPI document types `validFromInEpochSec` and `validToInEpochSec` as int64 integers, while the Go SDK types them as strings and the Python SDK sends them as strings.

positions.says: The contract enrollment certificate response has validFromInEpochSec as an int64.
The Go EnrollmentCert declares both validity fields as strings.
The Python create converts the validity window to epoch strings.

validity-epoch-types.impact: Go code that treats the value as an int64 fails; raw-HTTP callers follow the contract and read numbers. The contract has no enrollment certificate create or request body, so the Python position shows what is sent, not a disagreement with a contract request type.
